sources.title: Pierre Curie, with Autobiographical Notes
sources.by: Marie Curie (trans. Charlotte and Vernon Kellogg)
sources.quote_checked: There were no patents. We were working in the interests of science. Radium was not to enrich any one. Radium is an element. It belongs to all people. | We took out no patent and we did not reserve any advantage in any industrial exploitation. No detail was kept secret. | It was exhausting work to move the containers about, to transfer the liquids, and to stir for hours at a time, with an iron bar, the boiling material in the cast-iron basin. | It was only after treating one ton of pitchblende residues that I could get definite results. | The feeling of discouragement that sometimes came after some unsuccessful toil did not last long and gave way to renewed activity.

sources.title: Radium and the New Concepts in Chemistry (Nobel Lecture, December 11, 1911)
sources.quote_checked: To obtain a very pure salt I have had to perform several thousands of crystallizations. The progress of the fractionation is monitored by activity measurements. | Each chemical separation is followed by a measurement of the activity of the products obtained
